description:
The production throughput path gives every concurrent stream a separate
*cursor* on ONE shared underlying platform connection, not an independent
session. In benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py the connection_factory
closures (TPC-H lines 375-383, TPC-DS lines 244-252) call
`_make_stream_cursor(connection)` -> `connection.cursor()`
(benchbox/platforms/base/connection_wrappers.py:121-129) against the single
connection passed into the driver.

This is safe and intentional for DuckDB (its Python client is documented as
thread-safe at cursor level and cursors share the embedded DB), and the
DuckDB caveat is documented in docs/benchmarks/tpc-h.md. But TPC throughput
semantics model N INDEPENDENT concurrent users/sessions, and for
client/server engines a single connection is a single session:
- Many DB-API drivers (e.g. psycopg, Snowflake, Databricks SQL, Trino) do not
  support truly concurrent statement execution across cursors of one
  connection — calls serialize on the connection lock or raise.
- Even where they don't error, all streams share one session's server-side
  resources, so it is not a real multi-user concurrency measurement.

Fix: make the per-stream connection acquisition a platform capability. Engines
that model concurrency at the connection level (server engines) must hand each
stream its OWN connection/session from a factory or pool; embedded engines
(DuckDB) keep the cursor-sharing fast path. The throughput driver already
calls `connection_factory()` per stream (throughput_test.py) -- the gap is
that the adapter closure returns cursors of one connection instead of
independent sessions.

anti_patterns.dont: open N real connections for embedded DuckDB
anti_patterns.why: cursor sharing is the correct model there

preserves.behavior: Connections are still closed per stream in _execute_stream's finally block.
DuckDB throughput continues to use cursor sharing (documented, correct) with no perf regression.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/experimental/concurrency/executor.py:ConcurrentLoadExecutor — already calls connection_factory() per stream for independent connections; reuse its contract.
benchbox/experimental/concurrency/pool_tester.py:ConnectionPoolTester — an existing connection-pool abstraction to borrow the acquire/release shape from.
benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py — where per-platform connection creation lives; add a 'new independent connection for stream' hook.
benchbox/platforms/base/connection_wrappers.py:_make_stream_cursor — the current shared-cursor helper; needs a per-platform 'independent session' variant.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration -k throughput_session_isolation -v
verifications.expected: session-local state does not leak across streams

work_units.notes:
Added a hook (e.g. adapter.new_stream_connection()) with a default that
preserves today's DuckDB cursor behavior; server adapters override to open
a fresh connection/session per stream.

Implemented as StreamConnectionCapability (SHARED_CURSOR default /
INDEPENDENT_CONNECTION) in benchbox/platforms/base/connection_wrappers.py,
plus PlatformAdapter.stream_connection_capability (class attribute) and
PlatformAdapter.new_stream_connection() (the hook) in
benchbox/platforms/base/adapter.py. Base new_stream_connection() returns
_make_stream_cursor(connection) unchanged for SHARED_CURSOR; it raises
NotImplementedError for INDEPENDENT_CONNECTION unless a subclass overrides
it, so declaring the capability without an override fails fast instead of
silently reproducing the shared-session bug.
work_units.summary: Define a platform capability: per-stream independent connection vs shared-cursor, defaulting per engine

work_units.notes:
Both throughput connection_factory closures in
benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py (_execute_tpcds_throughput_test,
_execute_tpch_throughput_test) now call self.new_stream_connection(connection)
instead of _make_stream_cursor(connection) directly. The generic legacy
run_throughput_test()/_default_connection_factory path (execution.py ~1520,
not one of the two named closures and not on the production
_execute_queries_by_type dispatch path exercised by real benchmark runs)
was intentionally left unchanged - out of the TODO's named scope.
work_units.summary: Wire the throughput connection_factory closures to use the capability

work_units.notes:
Used SQLite-per-connection as the server-style stand-in (per the note's
own preference over Postgres/docker): tests/integration/test_throughput_session_isolation.py.
A CREATE TEMP TABLE (SQLite's connection-scoped, session-local construct)
set in one stream's independent connection is invisible from another's -
proving real session isolation. A companion pair of real-DuckDB tests
pins the SHARED_CURSOR default: a plain (non-TEMP) table created via one
stream's cursor is immediately visible via another's, proving they share
one connection/session with zero extra connections opened (the
anti_pattern this TODO forbids).
work_units.summary: Add a test proving streams get isolated sessions on a server-style engine (session-scoped setting does not leak across streams)
